tool_analysis:
Step Analysis:
The recorded steps show a full Magento 1.9 admin product edit workflow:
1) Navigate to the Manage Products grid URL; redirected to login.
2) Log into Magento admin with username/password.
3) Land on the Manage Products grid showing products, filters, pagination, and mass actions.
4) Click a per-row Edit link for a specific product (ID 2783) to open its edit form.
5) On the product edit page, edit fields on the General tab (Name, SKU, Status, Visibility).
6) Switch to the Prices tab and update Price and Tax Class.
7) Switch to the Inventory tab and update Qty and Stock Availability.
8) Switch to the Websites tab, toggle website assignment, then click Save to persist changes.
9) After saving, return to the Manage Products grid.

Task Definition:
Create a reusable tool that, given a target product identifier and new field values, will:
- Ensure we are on the Manage Products grid (authenticating if necessary).
- Open that product’s edit page from the grid.
- Update General, Prices, Inventory, and Websites fields with provided values.
- Save the product.
This tool must explicitly avoid brittle selectors like `#name` and instead rely on element hashes gathered from the session and robust actions. Where dynamic content is involved (tabs, post-save redirects), we include waits or agent steps that synchronize on visible labels/text rather than IDs.

Action Plan:
1) Navigation to grid:
   - Directly navigate to the Manage Products grid URL using a navigation step.
2) Login (if shown):
   - Use deterministic input steps against the username and password inputs captured by elementHash.
   - Click the Login button using its elementHash.
   - Include a short wait to allow redirect to complete.
3) Open product edit page from grid:
   - From the grid, click the per-row Edit link associated with the input `product_id` using an agent step, because the row index and element hash are product-specific and not stable across environments. The agent will locate the row whose ID cell text matches `{product_id}` and click its Edit link.
4) General tab edits:
   - Use deterministic input/select steps based on elementHash for:
     - Name (elementHash df3020a86b)
     - SKU (elementHash 1349f1ca81)
     - Status select (elementHash d7baed0536)
     - Visibility select (elementHash 2d6f7788e8)
   - Before these, add a short wait to ensure the General tab content is fully loaded after navigation, rather than waiting for `#name`.
5) Switch to Prices tab and edit:
   - Click the Prices tab link using elementHash 86ed7ee82d.
   - Wait for the Prices panel to load (by time-based wait; labels are static in Magento 1).
   - Input into the Price field (elementHash e457e89369).
   - Change Tax Class select (elementHash 1d20c0f068).
6) Switch to Inventory tab and edit:
   - Click the Inventory tab using elementHash 71d44f34a7.
   - Wait for panel.
   - Input Qty (elementHash 15f8e67c9f).
   - Change Stock Availability select (elementHash 09a76db7af).
7) Switch to Websites tab and adjust assignment:
   - Click the Websites tab using elementHash 3d30f36949.
   - Wait for panel.
   - Toggle Main Website checkbox using elementHash 12bd777a77 based on `website_assigned` input.
8) Save product:
   - Click Save button using elementHash 8677f5f4ee.
   - Wait a bit for redirect back to grid.
9) Optionally extract confirmation/message:
   - Use an extraction step to capture the success or error notice text (e.g., “The product has been saved.”) to return as `save_result`.

Variable Identification:
Core inputs derived from actions and real values:
- base_admin_url (string, required): Root URL to the Magento admin, e.g., `http://dockerized-magento.local/index.php`.
- username (string, required): Admin login username (demo used `admin`).
- password (string, required): Admin login password (demo used `password123`).
- product_id (string, required): Numeric product ID used in the grid’s ID column and edit URL segment (demo used `2783`).
- product_name (string, required): New Name value for the product (demo: “Erika Running Short 28 Purple - Automated Tool Demo v3”).
- product_sku (string, required): New SKU value (demo: “WSH12-28-PURPLE-TOOL-DEMO-V3”).
- status (string, required, enum: ["Enabled", "Disabled"]): Product status on General tab.
- visibility (string, required, enum: ["Not Visible Individually", "Catalog", "Search", "Catalog, Search"]): Visibility value.
- price (string, required): New base price numeric string in Prices tab (demo: “64.99”).
- tax_class (string, required, enum: ["None", "Taxable Goods", "Shipping", "Tax Exempt"]): Tax Class.
- qty (string, required): Inventory quantity value (demo: “200”).
- stock_availability (string, required, enum: ["In Stock", "Out of Stock"]).
- website_assigned (bool, optional, default true): Whether Main Website checkbox should be checked (`true`) or unchecked (`false`).

Step Optimization & URL Use:
- We keep an initial navigation step that goes straight to the grid URL, constructed from `base_admin_url` (e.g., `{base_admin_url}/admin/catalog_product/`). This is faster than clicking through the Admin menu.
- For opening a product edit page, we could directly navigate to `{base_admin_url}/admin/catalog_product/edit/id/{product_id}/`. However, the original task explicitly requires demonstrating the per-row Edit link, so we keep an agent step that clicks the Edit link, preserving the UX requirement.
- We avoid using brittle CSS IDs such as `#name`. Instead we rely on stable elementHash-backed deterministic steps captured in this run; these are resilient to dynamic attributes as long as DOM shape remains consistent.
- We insert explicit wait steps after navigation and tab switches, addressing prior timing issues where the tool tried to access an element before it existed.
- We keep the workflow single-purpose: editing an existing product. We do not include optional actions like filtering the grid, changing sort order, or using mass actions, even though the session explored them.

This design directly addresses the previous failure (waiting for `#name` on the edit page) by:
- Never referencing `#name` or similar fragile selectors.
- Using either elementHash-based deterministic steps or, where necessary, a short wait and/or agent step that synchronizes on visible text.
- Including waits after each major navigation (login redirect, product edit navigation, tab changes) to ensure content is ready before interacting.
name: tool_edit_product_v4
description: Open a Magento 1 product edit page from the Manage Products grid, modify key product fields across tabs (General, Prices, Inventory, Websites), and save the product, using stable selectors and waits that avoid the previous #name selector failure.

steps.description: Navigate directly to the Manage Products grid URL in the Magento admin.
Wait for potential redirect to login page or grid to complete.
Enter admin username into the username field on the login form using a generic text input selector; works because this is the only visible text input.
Enter admin password into the password field on the login form using the password input selector.
Click the Login button to authenticate and enter the admin panel.
Wait for login processing and redirect to the Manage Products grid to finish.
Use an agentic step because the specific row index and DOM positions change; selector must be based on product ID cell text and the per-row 'Edit' link.
steps.task: On the Manage Products grid, locate the row whose ID column text equals {product_id} and click its 'Edit' link in the Action column to open the product edit page.

steps.description: Wait for the product edit page for the selected product to fully load with the General tab active.
Update the Name field on the General tab for the product using a deterministic elementHash-based selector.
Update the SKU field on the General tab using its deterministic elementHash selector.
Set the Status select on the General tab to the desired value (Enabled or Disabled).
Set the Visibility select on the General tab to the desired option.
Click the Prices tab in the Product Information sidebar to show pricing fields.
Wait for the Prices tab content to become visible.
Update the Price field on the Prices tab with the new base price.
Set the Tax Class select on the Prices tab to the desired tax class.
Click the Inventory tab in the Product Information sidebar to show inventory fields.
Wait for the Inventory tab content to become visible.
Update the Qty field on the Inventory tab with the new inventory quantity.
Set the Stock Availability select on the Inventory tab (In Stock or Out of Stock).
Click the Websites tab in the Product Information sidebar to manage website assignments.
Wait for the Websites tab content to become visible.
Use an agent step to toggle the Main Website checkbox according to website_assigned, since exact checkbox id may vary across installations.
steps.task: On the Websites tab of the product edit page, ensure that the 'Main Website' checkbox reflects the desired assignment: checked if website_assigned is true, unchecked if website_assigned is false.

steps.description: Click the Save button to persist all product changes.
Wait for the save request to complete and redirect back to the Manage Products grid or stay on edit page with a confirmation message.
Capture the result of the save action for reporting back to the caller.
steps.goal: Extract any success or error messages related to the product save operation, such as 'The product has been saved.' or SQL/validation errors.

input_schema.name: base_admin_url
input_schema.description: Base Magento admin URL prefix without trailing slash, e.g. 'http://dockerized-magento.local/index.php'.

input_schema.name: username
input_schema.description: Magento admin username used on the login page.

input_schema.name: password
input_schema.description: Magento admin password used on the login page.

input_schema.name: product_id
input_schema.description: Numeric product ID to edit, matching the ID column in the grid and the /edit/id/{product_id}/ URL segment.

input_schema.name: product_name
input_schema.description: New Name value for the product on the General tab.

input_schema.name: product_sku
input_schema.description: New SKU value for the product on the General tab; should be unique in catalog.

input_schema.name: status
input_schema.description: General tab Status value controlling whether the product is enabled.

input_schema.name: visibility
input_schema.description: General tab Visibility value controlling catalog/search visibility.

input_schema.name: price
input_schema.description: New base Price value on Prices tab, as a numeric string in store currency (e.g. '64.99').

input_schema.name: tax_class
input_schema.description: Tax Class selection on Prices tab.

input_schema.name: qty
input_schema.description: New inventory Qty value on Inventory tab (integer-like string).

input_schema.name: website_assigned
input_schema.description: Whether the Main Website checkbox on the Websites tab should be checked (true) or unchecked (false).
